findings.detail: At clock low (t+0) the SV driver applies reset or enqueues at most one entry per channel. It then drives the head and valid=(tail>head). It samples ready at +4, before the edge at +5, and pops at most one head per channel after the edge, so the next head appears on the next cycle. TransportOracle.drive/advance mirrors this ordering. The oracle uses pre.ready, never post.ready. No lookahead, reordering or duplication path was found.

cmd_fire and tx_fire are computed from ready values sampled at +4, after the head is driven, so any combinational ready dependence on valid is captured as 'pre'. This matches the checker contract, which handshakes on pre ready&valid only. Post-edge values are logged but never used for acceptance.

Each asserted offer enqueues a new entry with ID=cycle, independent of payload. The unit test and the same_payload_two_offers_complete case show two TX IDs (8 and 9) accepted once each. The short variant is correctly reported as verification_complete=false.

With rst_n=0, both queues are cancelled (tail-head added to cancelled), visible payloads are zeroed, and valid=0, so no fire can occur in a reset cycle. Offers during reset are a fatal error in the SV driver and a ValueError in the validator. Accepted items are not reclassified as cancelled. The pending_queues_hardware_abort_restart case gives cancelled IDs cmd 9-12 and TX 11-25, and the conservation check holds. request_ids rejects partial cancellation.

The pre-loop #1 contains no clock edge. Each 22-field vector line produces exactly one TRACE, one posedge and one QUEUE line. The driver stops at EOF with no drain. parse enforces len(rows)==len(requests)==len(states), and the runtime requires DRIVER_OK steps=N. The pending EOF cases (tx_queue_pending_at_eof, pending_prefix) correctly keep delivery_complete=false even though the raw checker verdict is pass.

The SV fatal at cycle>=392 equals 8 + 6*64 exactly, and queue capacity 392 cannot overflow within that cycle cap. This works only because the budget is unchanged. Any budget change would silently need a driver change, and the freeze checks do not tie Capacity to the budget.

Any exception from simulate is logged as status 'simulation_failed' with only error_type recorded. That one label covers: transport-oracle mismatch (driver error), raw-denominator change, checker worker or selftest failure, and simulator crash. No message or stage is recorded, so driver errors cannot be cleanly separated from infrastructure faults. DUT failures do stay separate, as the checker verdict 'fail' with status 'simulated'. After a failure, the row reuses the stale prior round's coverage and checker fields, and the same happens for 'no_valid_actions'. These rows are labelled by status but could be misread.

The JSON schema enforces exact fields, widths, speed<=2, enable=1 and sw_reset=0. It does not encode the dummy-command ban, the non-Standard bidirectional ban or the no-offer-during-reset rule. validate() enforces all three, so model outputs that break them are counted as failed attempts, not silent repairs. A mid-run rst_n=0 is permitted and cancels pending offers. This is legal, but the contract should state it explicitly.

messages() reuses old[0], the historical INSTRUCTIONS system prompt, which is not in the packet. It most likely describes valid/tx_valid as direct pins that must be held until accepted. That would contradict the offer contract ('Do not repeat an offer merely to keep it valid'), and repeated offers would create duplicate transactions. The user payload also embeds the old pin contract and an execution_trace keyed by pin fields (input.valid). The rendered round-1 prompt must be reviewed before live B.

The packet contains 4 controls, all withdraw/change controls (cmd_valid, cmd_length, tx_valid, tx_data), plus unit tests for an edited accept ID and changed request intent. The preregistration requires deliberate dropped, changed and duplicate driver controls. The packet shows no explicit duplicate-acceptance control at the SV/trace level, and no dropped-offer control (an offer present in requests but absent from pins). It also shows no reordered-head or post-edge-ready-acceptance control.

TransportOracle and the SV driver share one author (GPT/Codex). The oracle is a separate re-implementation that checks the logged pins and ledger, which gives some protection, but it is not author-independent. Dual-simulator agreement of trace.json and transport.json hashes shows determinism across simulators, not correctness. result.json hashes differ between tools in every case; this is presumably the coverage and paths fields and should be documented.

Cumulative replay from the seed is deterministic by construction, since the same vectors run on a fresh simulation. pending_prefix shows a pending ID carried at EOF. The packet contains no artifact showing split-batch versus full-cumulative agreement across a round boundary with pending items, although the offline gate requires one.

The transport feedback strips command_accept_ids but still exposes cmd_accepted_ids, pending_ids and cancelled_ids through request_ids. That is harmless, but the future C and P message builders must emit byte-identical transport sections. Those builders do not exist in this version and cannot be checked.

The freeze hashes create_spi_core_safe_driver.py, preflight_spi_core_safe_driver.py and review_spi_core_safe_driver.py, plus pilot_model/run_midterm helpers. None of these are in the packet. The unit test also reads preflight-v1, while the evidence is preflight-v2. The preflight summary and case-definition contents (the 17-target reachability and seed-zero checks) were not supplied.

The checker sha256 07765601... matches the source hash listed in the packet. The runtime passes only actual pins to check_trace. The checker's pre-existing residual gaps (F1, F6, F7) carry over and are not fixed by this transport.

limitations: Read-only static review of the supplied packet; nothing was executed and no formal proof is claimed.
Simulation agreement and passing controls were not taken as evidence of checker or driver correctness.
The historical INSTRUCTIONS prompt, the preflight, create and review scripts, the preflight summary and the model client were not in the packet.
DUT RTL and calibration coverage counts were not supplied; target reachability and the seed-zero status of targets are unverified here.
Only one Verilator trace encoding was inspected; Icarus equality is asserted by hashes only.
Future C/P builders do not exist, so fairness across arms cannot be confirmed.
